title: Grateful Dead Live at Hartford Civic Center on 1982-04-18

ai_review.summary: A pristine 1982 Hartford soundboard captures a high‑energy show with a smoking second set (Space, Let It Grow, Big Railroad Blues) and crystal‑clear mix.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑balanced soundboard capture that sounds crisp and vivid, even when compared to the competing audience tape. The performance itself is often described as “unstoppable,” especially the second‑set jams – Space, Let It Grow, Big Railroad Blues, Samson and the rare Playing in the Band → Eyes of the World sequence – with Garcia ripping solos and Brent’s Hammond on fire.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive comments about both the musical performance (high‑energy, many standout songs) and the soundboard quality (crisp, well‑balanced), with only a few minor criticisms.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers praise a crisp, well‑balanced mix; some note the audience version sounds “underwater” in comparison, confirming the SBD is clear and free of major dropouts.

standout_songs: Playing in the Band > Eyes of the World (rare combo)
Sugar Magnolia > Playing in the Band
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set is solid and rocking, but the second set erupts into a monster performance with seamless transitions and rare song pairings that keep the momentum sky‑high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers call his solos “ripping” – especially the Let It Grow solo – and note his voice was in excellent form.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for a “totally spaced out Space,” his bass work described as “hysterical” and responsible for the famed “Earthquake” feeling.
band_member_comments.Bob: Commended for strong rhythm, slide work on Samson, and vocal delivery on Ship of Fools.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent highlighted for slashing on the Hammond during Big Railroad Blues and RxR Blues; keyboards noted as a key driver of the show’s power.
band_member_comments.Drums: The Rhythm Devils receive accolades for tight, powerful drumming leading into the space jam.
